Reference / net/tcp

net/tcp#

TCP connections and listeners.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let connection = await TcpConnecting(address: IpAddress("127.0.0.1"), port: 8080).connection();
defer connection.close();
await connection.output().write(request);
let reply = await connection.input().bytes(4096);

let listener = await TcpListening(port: 0).listener();
let port = listener::Local::port;
let accepted = await listener.connection();

Description#

TCP connections and listeners.

TcpEndpointRace and net/tcp_racing's TcpRacing try several addresses a little apart and keep the first to connect (Happy Eyeballs).

object TcpListeningOptions#

object TcpListeningOptions

Immutable listener request, to be applied before bind by the future listener. Defaults: no address reuse, no implicit dual stack, requested backlog 128. Backlog is non-negative and retained exactly; zero is valid. The OS can cap or reinterpret it, so this value does not observe the effective queue size. Unsupported settings are the consuming socket operation's responsibility.

TcpListeningOptions.TcpListeningOptions#

TcpListeningOptions()

Address reuse is on by default (SO_REUSEADDR, as Go does on Unix), so a restarted server binds its port while old connections sit in TIME_WAIT.

TcpListeningOptions.TcpListeningOptions#

TcpListeningOptions(address_reuse is bool, dual_stack is bool, backlog is int)

How a listener binds: address reuse, dual-stack, and a backlog of pending connections.

object TcpEndpointRace#

object TcpEndpointRace

The racing engine behind TcpRacing (net/tcp_racing) and TcpConnecting(host:, port:): RFC 8305 staggered attempts, first success wins.
